subject: Obligation to use a pre-existing genetic map

messages.author: e96592ac50954af8
messages.subject: Obligation to use a pre-existing genetic map
parts:
Dear Karl

We are wondering whether one actually needs to provide a genetic map for R/qtl2. We do have a physical map (SNP position) but no info on recombination rates so far.
Is it mandatory for a QTL analysis with R/qtl2 to dispose of a genetic map? Shall we duplicate our physical map file?

For now, we get a warning (gmap not present). 

Thank you
Marc

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Obligation to use a pre-existing genetic map
parts:
No it’s not required; that’s why you get a warning rather than an error. 

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Obligation to use a pre-existing genetic map
parts:
There is a function est_map() for re-estimating the inter-marker distances, similar to est.map() in R/qtl1. It doesn't work for all cross types but it should work for most of them.

I would like to add more facilities for diagnosing problems with marker order, but I don't expect to include many or any facilities for de novo map construction.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Re: Obligation to use a pre-existing genetic map
parts:
est_map() should work for the MAGIC lines with cross type "riself8". It hasn't yet been implemented for cross types "ail", "ail3", "dh6", "do", "dof1", "genail", "genril", or "hs".

But if you have high-density genotype data, you may not need a high-quality genetic map in order to calculate genotype probabilities. Re-scaling the physical map an estimate of the overall cM/Mb ratio may be sufficient.

karl
